name: Rwanda
summary_text: Rwanda demands real caution from trans visitors. Same-sex intimacy is not criminalised, and the government formally tolerates a small LGBT presence — but a 2025 Human Rights First Rwanda Association submission to the UN Human Rights Committee documents ongoing law-enforcement abuses against transgender persons, including arbitrary arrests and detentions (framed as “vagrancy” or “deviance” round-ups in Kigali's periodic street-cleaning operations). There is no legal gender recognition, no anti-discrimination protection, and civil society operates within the regime's tight limits. For a visitor: no statutory exposure, but Kigali's sweep operations can net gender-nonconforming people, and recourse is nil.

sources.title: Rwanda | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex intimacy is not criminalised in Rwanda, but the Human Rights First Rwanda Association's 2025 UN submission highlighted law-enforcement abuses against trans people - harassment during identity checks and arbitrary arrests on 'vagrancy' or 'public order' grounds. Rainbow Migration reported in 2022 that Rwanda is 'now a source country' for people seeking UK asylum based on sexual orientation. LGBTIQ organisations cannot register openly; activists held a public Pride event in 2023.

sources.title: Rwanda’s Transgender Community Face Violent Detentions For Being Trans
sources.claim_summary: VICE World News (Nov 2020): 'Rwanda's Transgender Community Face Violent Detentions For Being Trans' - Bella, a singer, was detained by Kigali police on Christmas Day 2018 despite showing her work card; police falsely asserted she was homeless and sold drugs - documenting violent detentions of trans Rwandans.

Rwanda Official Gazette No. Special (15 Oct 2021): Law No. 058/2021 relating to the protection of personal data and privacy - the data-protection statute relevant to privacy protections (trilingual Kinyarwanda/English/French).

sources.title: Homosexuality isn't our Problem-Says President Kagame - KT PRESS
sources.claim_summary: KT Press (Sept 2016): President Kagame on LGBT life in Rwanda: 'it hasn't been our problem. And we don't intend to make it our problem'; Article 26 of the constitution recognises only civil monogamous marriage between a man and a woman; Rwanda eliminated the criminalisation provision from its draft code in 2010 and signed two UN SOGI resolutions - the only African nation to do so.

AP (Sep 2019): 'Rwandan gospel singer comes out as gay, to country's shock' — prominent gospel artist Albert Nabonibo's coming-out interview and the backlash in a country where same-sex relations are criminal.

sources.title: The Queerstory Files: Gay in the Great Lakes of Africa
sources.claim_summary: The Queerstory Files (Oct 2012): 'Gay in the Great Lakes of Africa' - anthropologists say homosexuality was widespread among young men in both Tutsi and Hutu of pre-colonial Rwanda and Burundi, always private and secret - historical context for Rwanda.
